notices.format: No type size is set; must be included within the contract; gives the MHIC telephone numbers 410-230-6231 and 1-888-218-5925 and website https://www.labor.maryland.gov/license/mhic/, and states that mediation, the Guaranty Fund and the right to ask for a performance bond are available
notices.support: Neither Bus. Reg. 8-501(c)(1)(viii) and (ix) nor COMAR 09.08.01.26 sets a type size for the MHIC notice.
notices.summary_row: MHIC consumer notice (mediation, Guaranty Fund, performance bond)
notices.hold_reason: no prescribed wording; the regulation only lists what the notice must state (mediation, Guaranty Fund, performance bond) and the statute only requires the MHIC phone number and website

notices.trigger: Door-to-door sale of $25 or more, including a sale after the buyer's invitation, made away from the seller's place of business; for a home improvement contract the period is five business days, seven if the buyer is at least 65
notices.format: Statement in boldface of at least 10 points next to the buyer's signature space, plus a Notice of Cancellation form in duplicate in 10 point boldface; for a home improvement contract the form is on a separate sheet that is not part of the contract; oral notice; same language as the sales talk
notices.support: For a home improvement contract 14-302.1(2)(i) says it shall "Be on a separate form that is not a part of the home improvement contract". The separate-form rule controls for home improvement.
notices.summary_row: Door-to-door statement beside the signature; Notice of Cancellation form
notices.hold_reason: The 14-302 statement and form are worded with THREE business days, but a home improvement contract must allow five business days (seven if the buyer is at least 65) under 14-302.1, and the statute does not print the substituted wording ('The drafter therefore changes ...'); printing the three-day wording would be wrong, and changing the numbers would be retyping. Held.

notices.summary_row: Mortgage or lien and rescission notice (10 point bold, first page, initials)
notices.block: 1. Bus. Reg. 8-501, home improvement contract contents (the full section)
notices.start: This contract creates a mortgage or lien
notices.quote_note: Excluded: the statute's opening curly quotation mark before 'This contract creates' and the closing curly quotation mark after 'rescinding the contract.' (the sentence's own period is inside the quote and is included).
notices.boundary_unsure: none: set off by quotation marks after 'in substantially the following form'. Stored on file, not printed: it applies only when payment is secured by residential real estate, which the builder does not know. The statute also requires it in not smaller than 10 point bold type on the first page of the contract and independently initialed by the homeowner (8-501(c)(3)); those are formatting duties, not text.

notices.title: Signed acknowledgment of the right to cancel (oral notice)
notices.trigger: Home improvement contract sold away from the seller's place of business; the buyer signs it and gets a copy with the contract
notices.format: Signed by the buyer; a copy goes to the buyer with the completed contract; includes a check box for a buyer who is at least 65
notices.support: the seller must "Obtain the signature of the buyer on the following written acknowledgment" and "Furnish to the buyer a copy of the written acknowledgment of the buyer’s right to cancel with the completed receipt or copy of the home improvement contract."
notices.summary_row: HOME IMPROVEMENT override: five business days (seven if the buyer is 65 or older), separate cancellation form, signed acknowledgment of oral notice
notices.hold_reason: the block is the whole section 14-302.1 with operative rules around the acknowledgment, and the official page serves the check box before 'check if buyer is at least 65 years old' as a literal question mark

changes.new: Three business days (CL 14-302) for door-to-door sales that are not home improvement; five business days, seven if the buyer is at least 65, for a home improvement contract (CL 14-302.1); oral notice with a signed acknowledgment, two copies
changes.support: Three business days remains the rule only for door-to-door sales that are not home improvement contracts (for example house cleaning sold at the home).

changes.new: Home improvement contracts: five business days, or seven if the buyer is at least 65. Other door-to-door sales: three. A business day is any calendar day except Sunday or the listed holidays, so Saturday counts.
One third of the contract price at or before signing; no payment before the contract is signed (BR 8-617)
changes.support: A person may not receive a deposit of more than one-third of the home improvement contract price before or at the time of execution of the home improvement contract.

shall allow the buyer to cancel a transaction prior to midnight of the fifth business day after the date of the transaction

changes.new: Door-to-door act (CL 14-302 and 14-302.1: five business days, seven if the buyer is at least 65, separate cancellation form, signed acknowledgment of oral notice) even for invited visits
changes.support: The first pass missed section 14-302.1 entirely.

unsure: MD-mhic: the notice has to be inside the contract, but the state gives only a list of required content and no fixed sentence, so nothing is loaded.
MD-cancel: the 14-302 statement and form are the wording to print, but a home improvement contract needs five or seven days instead of three, which the statute does not print.
MD-oral-ack: added as a new notice because the law hands the signed acknowledgment over with the contract; held because of the damaged check box character.

cancellation.business_days set to 5: 14-302.1 gives home improvement contracts five business days (seven if the buyer is at least 65, kept in the notes); the 3-day rule remains only for non-home-improvement door-to-door sales such as house cleaning.

MD-security: stored on file only, never printed, because it applies only when payment is secured by residential real estate; it must also be in 10 point bold on the first page and initialed by the homeowner.
